title: The gate job runs after the proof run is attested, and its next run for the commit reads that attestation from the store
when: Reads the proof run workflow's gate job. Then, in a fixture repository, assure gate change runs for a change whose store keeps no attestation yet; the attest job then keeps a passed proof run for the commit, and assure gate change runs again.
then: The gate job needs the attest job, runs on every pull request also when the suites or the attest job fail, and not when the run is cancelled, may only read the repository, pins every action to a commit, installs no package the change names, checks out the change's commit with its full history, builds assure from the pull request's base commit, and runs that binary in the change's checkout as assure gate change with the commit, the pull request's base and the Lathe the workflow builds. When a step before the gate fails, or Lathe or assure does not build, the job says that the gate did not run. The first run is refused with no verified proof run. The second run passes, and its decision rests on that attestation. The store is asked for the change's commit at each run.

title: The image build hears Application built, reads the build record at its digest, and builds from the recorded executable only
when: With the result of a real build that the stego binary made, and the Application built event that stego build printed: stego image build --after runs with that event and the result folder; then with events that name another executable, another build record and another revision, and with an executable given beside the event.
then: The first run builds the image of the build record and the executable the event names, and prints Image built with the image digest and the build record digest. Each other run is refused, names the digest or the revision that differs or says that the executable comes from the event only, and leaves no image folder.
notes: It runs the stego binary that the shared fixture builds once per test run from a clean snapshot of the tree, on the one real application build of the fixture. It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: Sign the image hears Image built, reads the image record at the built digest, and signs that digest with the trusted signer
when: With a copy of the image that the stego binary built from the real build, the Image built event that stego image build printed, and SBOM attestation bundles about the image digest by the trusted signer, which a fake GitHub CLI prints as gh attestation verify does: stego image sign --after runs; then with events that name another image and another build record, and with bundles by another signer.
then: The first run writes the signature record of the image digest and the image record digest by the trusted signer with both SBOM attestations, and prints Image signed with the image digest and the signer. Each other run is refused, names the digest that differs or says the signature is not by the trusted signer, and writes no signature record.
notes: It runs the stego binary that the shared fixture builds once per test run, on the image of the fixture's one real build. A real keyless signature needs a CI identity, so the bundles are verification results that a fake gh prints; STEGO's own signature checks run on them. It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: Publish the image hears Image signed, checks the signature again, and publishes only an image whose signature verifies
when: With a copy of the fixture image that stego image sign signed, the Image signed event that it printed, the same bundles, and an in-process TLS registry with basic auth that counts its requests: stego image publish --after runs; then with an unsigned copy, events that name another image and another signer, bundles by another signer, a signature record whose log entry was changed, and no signature flags.
then: The first run publishes the image, writes the publication record of the image digest at the explicit repository, and prints Image published. Each other run is refused, names the missing signature, the digest or signer that differs, the signature that does not verify, the record that differs from it or the missing flag, writes no publication record, and sends the registry no request.
notes: It runs the stego binary that the shared fixture builds once per test run, on the image of the fixture's one real build. The bundles are verification results that a fake gh prints. Publication without --after checks the signature too (ST-BLD-UC06-R01-T01). It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass.

title: The qualify-release job hears the published release in the same run and qualifies it with its passed decision through the consumer path
when: Reads the qualify-release job of proof-run.yml, then runs the publish-release job and the qualify-release job with the release output; then publishes again and removes the release decision before the qualify-release job runs; then runs the job with a release output that names another release, with no checks run at the commit, and with a checks run that completes at the second look.
then: The job needs publish-release, may only read, checks out the commit and runs qualify-compiler-release.py --verify-release for it. The first qualification passes and its record names the decision and the release; the second fails, names the missing release decision, and writes no record. Another release name fails before qualification; no checks run fails at once and says so; the job waits for the checks run in progress and then qualifies.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: The publish-release job hears the attest-release job of the same run, and publishes for a passed decision only
when: Reads the publish-release and attest-release jobs of proof-run.yml, then runs the publish-release job for a passed decision and for a refused one.
then: The publish-release job needs attest-release and has its condition, passed is true; the passed decision publishes, and the refused one publishes nothing.
notes: The test runs the job's steps with bash as GitHub Actions does, with a fake gh at the edge that answers from fixed records, and the real jq, unzip and coreutils. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: After a digest is withdrawn, the next delivery check refuses an image whose build record pins it, naming the digest and the advisory
when: With the hosted image of the test data set, whose build record pins the component digest D: stego delivery check runs; then the registry copy gets the advisory A1, which withdraws a digest that the build record does not pin, and the check runs again; then the registry copy gets the advisory A2, which withdraws D, and the check runs again on the same image.
then: Expects the first and the second run to pass. Expects the third run to exit non-zero, naming D and A2, and not naming A1.
notes: The check must read the advisories at its run, not from a copy that it kept: the test runs the same binary on the same image before and after each advisory is added. The advisory A1 is the case that catches a check that refuses on any advisory, not on one that withdraws a digest the record pins.

title: A published image is checked against the delivery policy from its build record and its referrers, and is refused when one check fails
when: With the two images of the test data set in the local registry: stego delivery check runs on each published digest; then on a copy of the hosted image with its CycloneDX SBOM referrer removed, and on a copy signed with a test key that is not a trusted signer.
then: Expects both images to pass, with the output naming the build record and each referrer that the check read at the digest. Expects each copy to exit non-zero, naming the policy check that failed: the missing SBOM referrer, and the signer that is not trusted.
notes: In the local registry, the tag latest points at the other image, so that a check that reads the record or the referrers by tag, not at the published digest, is caught. The second sentence of the policy, that the platform's gate enforces the same policy, waits for ST-DLV-Q02; this test proves the pipeline's half only.

title: The run that writes the Kubernetes base also writes the delivery object, or says in the plan that it writes none
when: With the service of the test data set: stego apply runs; then, in a new copy of the service without its delivery stanza, stego apply runs.
then: Expects the first run to write the Kubernetes base and the ApplicationSet, and the generation record of that run to list both files. Expects the second run to write the Kubernetes base and no delivery object, and its plan to say that no delivery object is written because the declaration has no delivery stanza.
notes: The policy text says Argo CD Application; the delivery object is an ApplicationSet, as decided in ST-DLV-Q01 and stated in ST-DLV-A4 and ST-DLV-UC07-R04. The test expects the ApplicationSet. The stego binary runs as a child process from a test in cmd/stego, with the project folder of the test data set as its working folder.

title: After a supersession, the next plan in each service reports the pin's standing, and refuses it past its date unless overridden
when: With two services in temporary folders that pin digest DA1, with their registry pin at the commit before the supersession: a supersession of DA1 by DA2 with a fail date ahead is recorded at the registry's head, and stego plan runs in each service; then the fail date passes, and stego plan runs in each service, without and with an override of the pin by name.
then: Expects the first plan in each service to exit 0 and to name DA1, its successor DA2 and the fail date. Expects the plan without an override to exit non-zero and name DA1 in each service, and the plan with the override to go on.
notes: It shows that the lifecycle is read from the registry's head, not from the pinned snapshot. The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam. The option of stego plan and stego apply that overrides one pin by name, with its reason, is not named yet (ST-GEN-CLI01 takes no flag today). The builder names it.

title: After a withdrawal, the next plan in each service refuses the pin past its date, naming the digest, the reason and the date, unless overridden
when: With two services in temporary folders that pin digest DB1: a withdrawal of DB1 with the reason 'leaks a token in a log' is recorded at the registry's head, the fail date passes, and stego plan runs in each service, without and with an override of the pin by name.
then: Expects the plan without an override to exit non-zero in each service and to name DB1, the reason and the fail date. Expects the plan with the override to go on.
notes: A plan before the fail date waits on ST-DIS-Q01. The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam. The option of stego plan and stego apply that overrides one pin by name, with its reason, is not named yet (ST-GEN-CLI01 takes no flag today). The builder names it.
